Hey all,

the condition has length > 1 "

I have run the microclimate model as instructed on this webpage from page 22-28.... 

https://www.ecography.org/sites/ecography.org/files/appendix/ecog-02360.pdf 

 but then when i input the ectotherm info from this webpage  ......

https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/ectotherm-model-tutorial 

from the 'plotting some output' section i just get the above error code. is this a common problem or am i doing something stupid? 

Thanks for any help, Ben

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Error in if (alpha_sub < 0 | alpha_sub > 1) { : the condition has length > 1
parts:
Hi Ben,

Try running it like this (if you're using the latest version from github you will need to un-comment some of the inputs because there have been some updates to what the ectotherm model needs):

ecto <- ectotherm(nyears = nyears,
                  minshades = rep(minshade, length(RAINFALL)),
                  maxshades = rep(maxshade, length(RAINFALL)),
                  alpha_sub = (1 - REFL),
                  DEP = DEP,
                  #KS = KS[seq(1, 19, 2)],
                  #b = BB[seq(1, 19, 2)],
                  #PE = PE[seq(1, 19, 2)],
                  metout = micro$metout,
                  shadmet = micro$shadmet,
                  soil = micro$soil,
                  shadsoil = micro$shadsoil,
                  soilmoist = micro$soilmoist,
                  shadmoist = micro$shadmoist,
                  humid = micro$humid,
                  shadhumid = micro$shadhumid,
                  soilpot = micro$soilpot,
                  shadpot = micro$shadpot,
                  #tcond = micro$tcond,
                  #shadtcond = micro$shadtcond,
                  rainfall = RAINFALL,
                  #rainhr = rep(-1,nrow(micro$metout)),
                  #preshr = rep(101325 * ((1 - (0.0065 * as.numeric(ALTT) / 288)) ^ (1/0.190284)), nrow(metout)),
                  elev = as.numeric(ALTT),
                  longitude = longlat[1],
                  latitude = longlat[2])

The ectotherm model when run with default inputs expects the output of one of the 'micro_xxx' functions (e.g. 'micro_global') that has the name 'micro'. Those 'micro_xxx' function are wrappers that set the microclimate model inputs up for different data sets, e.g. the NCEP or ERA5 or terraclimate data sets (micro_ncep, micro_era5, micro_terra). The way you ran the microclimate model, from that example, was more 'under the hood' where you specify all the inputs explicitly and you can include your own local weather data. But it was missing the step where the final list of outputs is put together in the way the ectotherm model wants them.

Hope that all makes sense. I set it up this way to make it easy to run the ectotherm model after running one of the 'micro_' functions, but if you set it up more manually you need to add a bit more code to properly feed in the input data.

All the best,
Mike
